caseno: Appeal from Appellate Decree No. 105 of 1987.
lawyer:
MI Farooque with Saleemullah ----- For the Appellant.
Zia-Ur-Rahman Khan ----- For the Respondent.
parties:
Motiul Hoque ----- Appellant
Vs.
Dhaka Improvement Trust (RAJUK) & another ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
15. Now let us deal with the point regarding the service of notice on the plaintiff terminating his lease. The lease is said to have been determined by a letter of the defendant No. 1 on 30.1.75 vide Ext. C. Mr. Farooqui argues the though the letter was shown to have been served on the plaintiff he could not have been imputed with the knowledge of the same unless it could be shown that the notice was tendered to or thereafter either received or returned being refused by the addressee. It is also argued that there cannot be any presumption of service of notice when the notice is found to have been returned with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon on the registered cover containing the notice. The learned Advocate also submits that after the liberation war period the plaintiff had to move from one place to another for his residence and, therefore, the return of the letter to the sender with the endorsement 'not known' cannot be treated as a good service and the plaintiff cannot be said to have knowledge of the forfeiture of his lease hold interest in the suit land. Mr. Zia-ur-Rahman Khan by way of referring to the section 27 of the General Clauses Act submits that the registered notice sent by post carries with it. the strong presumption of service of same if the notice is properly addressed and posted, unless this presumption is rebutted by cogent evidence. He submits that in the instant case the notice was admittedly issued by registered post with proper address but the presumption of due service was not rebutted as the notice was found to have been returned to the addressee with the endorsement Not know', by the postal peon. The provision of section 27 of the General Clauses Act which is relevant for the purpose reads as follows: 

 "It is true that the presumption raised by section 27 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 is a rebuttable one. But a mere denial to the effect that the notice was not received by him is not sufficient to rebut the presumption" and "Notice sent by registered post returned with the endorsement 'Left' on the registered cover by the postman although at the material time the addressee was residing at the particular address—presumption is that the notice was duly tendered to the addressee and the addressee must be fixed with constructive notice." 

 20. In the case of Dr. Jamshed Bakht Vs. Md. Kamaluddin reported in 1981 BO) 97 it was held that mere denial of receipt of the notice by the addressee or that the notice was not tendered to him is not sufficient to rebut the presumption of the service of notice by registered post as provided in section 27 of the General Clauses Act. The fact that the address of the plaintiff was given in the deed of lease as 13/12 Babar Road, Mohammadpur which also finds support from the subsequent affidavit sworn by the plaintiff vide Ext. 10(a) 10(b) and the plaintiff having not ever intimated about the change of his address leads us to the presumption that 13/12 Babar Road was the address of the plaintiff and this presumption having not been rebutted in any way by the defendant we are of view that the notice under registered cover was sent and properly addressed to the plaintiff. Though there is minor factual difference between the case where the notice under registered cover was returned to the sender with the endorsement 'left' and the present case where a letter under registered cover has been returned with the endorsement 'not known' by the postal peon the nature, intention and purpose, the mode applied and the effect in both the cases are virtually the same so far it relates to the service of notice. As we have already found from the record that the letter was properly addressed and the cover containing the notice was sent by registered post to the plaintiff to his address given by himself in the deed of agreement by the plaintiff and the said place of residence of the plaintiff being his last known place of residence, we hold that the presumption arises that the notice was duly tendered to the addressee and the said presumption having not been rebutted the addressee must be fixed with constructive notice.
